subject: [hw] IK->lead: header defect in redwood_vcodec.h (RWVC_DMA_SHARE does not exist) + client identity question
body:
Two items on the frozen header, no workaround applied silently:

1) DEFECT: line 58 says a handle "may be shared with the other minor by RWVC_DMA_SHARE", but no RWVC_DMA_SHARE ioctl/number is defined; struct rwvc_dma_alloc.flags bit 0 is the only sharing control ("flags bit 0: shared with the other minor"). Proposed text: replace "by RWVC_DMA_SHARE (server -> names a client buffer or vice versa is not needed: handles are global, access is checked against \"allocated by this file or shared to this minor\")" with "by flags bit 0 at RWVC_DMA_ALLOC (handles are global; access is checked against \"allocated by this file, or allocated with flags bit 0 and the accessor is on the other minor\")", and add "#define RWVC_DMA_SHARED 1u". Until then I define RWVC_DMA_SHARED 1u locally in nord2_vcodec_relay.inc and implement exactly that rule.

2) DESIGN LIMIT (please confirm it is acceptable): XNU cdevsw d_open/d_close/d_ioctl receive only (dev_t, ..., struct proc *); there is no per-open file pointer (spec_vnops.c:353). So a relay "client" can only be identified by process. Two fds in one process share one client id; close notification fires at the last close of the process. The VT plug-in is one process, vcodecd is the only minor-0 user, and the host test models 3 client processes, so I propose this as the semantics. Alternative would be a clone minor per open, which contradicts the frozen "minor 1 = redwood-vcodec-client" and needs an open handshake the ABI does not have.
